Script.name: helpwin
Script.script:
--[[ Help window Sean Stoves, 2026-08-02
Help files out of the scrollback and into a panel that starts empty every time you read one, so the last thing you asked about is the only thing in front of you.
Aardwolf will mark its own help output if you ask it to. Telnet channel 102 carries the tag options, one byte for which and one for on/off:
IAC SB 102 <option> <1 on | 2 off> IAC SE
Option 3 is helpfiles. With it on, the MUD wraps replies in its tag protocol - {help}...{/help}, and {helpsearch}...{/helpsearch} for 'help search' - so there's nothing to scrape. Without it every help is a wall of dashes with no machine-readable start or end, and the dash count moves with your screen width.
Mudlet has sendTelnetChannel102() for the wrapper, so we only supply the two payload bytes.
Paged, not scrolled. A Mudlet console that is scrolled up splits into a scrollback pane and a live pane with a divider across it - that split IS what being scrolled up looks like, and nothing turns it off. Right for the MUD window, where you want to keep reading while new text arrives. Wrong for a document, which has an end and doesn't move.
So the whole file goes into an invisible buffer and the panel shows one screenful copied out of it. Never scrolled, so never split, and page one is the top of the file. Resizing re-pages against the new height.
The buffer is also what keeps the colours: copy() and appendBuffer move a line with its formatting intact, the same trick the panel manager uses to carry a scrollback across a dock/embed flip.
30_tags.lua owns the tag gag and would otherwise treat {help} as an unknown marker and delete the wrapper itself. Two owners deleting the same line is what left blank gaps in the room description, so help is in its OWNED set there and this file is the only thing that touches it. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.helpwin = aardkit.helpwin or {}
local HW = aardkit.helpwin local U = aardkit.util.named("Help")
local CFG = U.load("helpwin", { on = true, -- Unlike search and shop this defaults to hiding the original. A help file -- is a wall of text you asked for by name and don't want in your -- scrollback; the other two are reports worth keeping in the log. 'helpwin -- gag' flips it either way. gag = true, })
-- declared ahead of the closures below so it binds this local rather than a -- global of the same name, which is nil forever local panel
--- -- asking the MUD to mark it ---
local HELPS_OPT = 3
-- Mudlet wraps this in IAC SB 102 ... IAC SE for us; the payload is the option -- and whether we want it. Wrapped because a Mudlet without it is a nil call, -- and a client that can't negotiate should still load the rest of the module. local function telopt(on) if not U.has("sendTelnetChannel102") then return false end return (pcall(sendTelnetChannel102, string.char(HELPS_OPT, on and 1 or 2))) end
function HW.negotiate() if not CFG.on then return end -- the MUD forgets between sessions, so this goes out on every connect telopt(true) end
--- -- panel ---
panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "help", title = "Help", width = 700, height = 460, x = "120px", y = "60px", fontSize = 10, -- put up by a help file arriving and by nothing else. Where and how big it -- is still persists - Adjustable.Container saves that itself on exit and -- reloads it by name; it's only whether it's showing that gets forced. transient = true, -- a taller panel is more lines per page, so the page gets recut onresize = function() if aardkit.helpwin.panel then aardkit.helpwin.panel:page_paint() end end, onbuild = function() if aardkit.helpwin.panel then aardkit.helpwin.panel.pagebtn = {} end end, })
HW.panel = panel
--- -- capture ---
local capturing, trig, timer
local function stop() if trig then pcall(killTrigger, trig); trig = nil end if timer then pcall(killTimer, timer); timer = nil end capturing = nil end
-- Armed on the open tag and killed on the close, rather than a permanent -- catch-all that tests a flag on every line of the session. The closing tag is -- recognised in here too: a second trigger for it would race this one, and -- whichever fired first would delete the line out from under the other. local function arm(kind) trig = tempRegexTrigger([[^.*$]], function() local line = getCurrentLine() or "" if line:match("^%s*{/help") then if CFG.gag then U.gag() end stop() panel:page_end() return end -- Not every tag is a line of its own. {helpkeywords} arrives welded to -- the front of the keywords line, so gagging by line would take the -- text with it - strip the tag off the line and keep the rest. local tag = line:match("^%s*(%b{})") if tag then if pcall(selectString, tag, 1) then pcall(replace, "") end end panel:page_add() if CFG.gag then U.gag() end end) -- a help that never closes would eat the rest of the session timer = tempTimer(15, function() if capturing then stop() U.warn("Help: no closing tag arrived - stopped capturing.") end end) capturing = kind end
function HW.on_open(kind) if not CFG.on then return end stop() if CFG.gag then U.gag() end panel:page_begin() panel:show() arm(kind or "help") end
--- -- commands ---
function HW.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) -- 'x opacity 200' where somebody looks for it, rather than only -- 'panel x opacity 200'. One line; core does the work. if aardkit.panel.verb("help", verb, rest) then return end
rest = U.trim(rest):lower()
if verb == "toggle" then panel:toggle()
elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then CFG.on = (verb == "on") U.save("helpwin", CFG) telopt(CFG.on) if not CFG.on then stop() end U.ok("Help window " .. verb .. (CFG.on and " - help goes to the panel." or " - help stays in the main window."))
elseif verb == "gag" then CFG.gag = not CFG.gag U.save("helpwin", CFG) U.ok("Help: " .. (CFG.gag and "panel only - the file is hidden from the main window." or "in both places."))
elseif verb == "next" then aardkit.panel.page_next("help") elseif verb == "prev" then aardkit.panel.page_prev("help")
elseif verb == "clear" then panel:page_begin() panel:page_paint() U.ok("Help window cleared.")
elseif verb == "retry" or verb == "negotiate" then if telopt(true) then U.ok("Asked the MUD to tag help output again.") else U.warn("This Mudlet has no sendTelnetChannel102 - can't negotiate.") end
elseif verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" or verb == "show" or verb == "hide" then aardkit.panel.cmd("help " .. verb .. (rest ~= "" and (" " .. rest) or ""))
else U.help("Help window", { { "helpwin toggle", "show or hide the panel" }, { "state", CFG.on and "on" or "off" }, { "showing", (panel.total or 0) > 0 and ((panel.total) .. " lines, page " .. (panel.page or 1) .. " of " .. (panel.pages or 1)) or "nothing yet" }, { "tagging", U.has("sendTelnetChannel102") and "'help negotiate' - never automatic" or "unavailable in this Mudlet" }, { "" }, { "helpwin", "show or hide the panel" }, { "helpwin on | off", "capture help, or leave it in the main window" }, { "helpwin gag", "hide it from the main window, or show it in both" }, { "helpwin next | prev", "page through the file, same as the buttons" }, { "helpwin clear", "empty it" }, { "helpwin retry", "ask the MUD to tag help output again" }, { "helpwin dock | embed | show | hide", "panel placement" }, { "helpwin opacity <0-255>", "how solid this window is; 'default' follows the shared setting" }, { "" }, { "Read help as you always have - 'help <topic>'. Aardwolf marks" }, { "the reply and it lands here instead of the scrollback." }, }) end end
aardkit.register("helpwin", "help files in their own panel, fresh each read", HW.cmd)
U.killhandler(aardkit_helpwin_connect) aardkit_helpwin_connect = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", function() stop() -- Nothing goes to the MUD here. This used to negotiate the help tags on -- connect - first behind a 2s timer, which landed squarely in the password -- prompt, then behind U.ready, which was correct and still not the point. -- Nothing in this suite talks to the MUD on its own account at login now. -- -- The cost: the MUD forgets the tag between sessions, so until you run -- 'help negotiate' the help files come through untagged and unpanelled. -- One command a session against a login that can't be eaten is the right -- side of that trade. end)
